extracted.intended_audience: journalists, media professionals, and readers interested in the future of journalism and journalism innovation
extracted.subtask_short: about page for a journalism lab
extracted.subtask_description: An organizational 'About' page describing the mission, staff, licensing, fellowship deadlines, and ways to follow or reuse the Nieman Journalism Lab's work. Not a how-to or formal guideline but a statement of purpose and reuse rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission / editorial focus
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nieman Journalism Lab's purpose is to help journalism figure out its future in an Internet age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains specific aims: highlight attempts at innovation and figure out what makes them succeed or fail; find good ideas for others to steal; help reporters and editors adjust to online work; help traditional news organizations find a way to survive; help new startups that will complement or supplant them. Framing is explicitly collaborative and investigative into what works online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader contributions / collaborative exchange
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary among them are our readers; we hope your contributions will make the Lab a collaborative exchange of ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invitation to the audience to 'Tell us what’s happening around you, or what should be.' Implies the Lab values reader-submitted tips, examples of innovation, and discussion that furthers understanding of journalism's evolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nieman Fellowship application deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual deadline to apply for a Nieman Fellowship: December 15 for international journalists and January 31 for Americans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirement for prospective fellowship applicants; included in the About/Foundation description as the standard annual application deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise noted, all content on this site is © the President and Fellows of Harvard College or the content’s original author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States default copyright ownership and sets up the following licensing terms. Indicates that some items may be exceptions if otherwise noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative Commons reuse policy (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 US)
rubrics_metrics.description: Also unless otherwise noted, all content on this site is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-Noncommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 United States License.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions: (a) you are not using it for commercial purposes; (b) you attribute it to the Nieman Journalism Lab and/or the work’s author, preferably with a link back to the original content; and (c) you release any work you build on top of our work under a similar license. Examples of allowed uses given: translating the entire site into Portuguese; redistributing posts to students in a college course; using the Twitter feed as lyrics in a song. Also: 'If you would like to use our work for any other use, feel free to get in touch.'

rubrics_metrics.name: How to cite Nieman Lab content
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested citation formats for the About page (MLA, APA, Chicago) are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given verbatim in MLA, APA, and Chicago formats, with full bibliographic elements and a URL. This provides standard guidance for academic or formal citation of site content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ways to follow and engage with the Lab
rubrics_metrics.description: The site lists channels for following the Lab: daily email, weekly email option, Twitter, Facebook, iPhone app, RSS, and subscription via email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages subscriptions and social follows as the primary means to 'follow how the news is changing' and receive Lab content; presents a 'daily email' as the best way for freshest coverage and offers a weekly alternative.
